intent: To demonstrate that a majority of Americans believe there is too much economic inequality in the United States.

units.meaning: The largest substantive survey response is 'Too much' economic inequality, selected by 61% of respondents.

basis.note: 61% is the largest value among the three substantive response categories.

accepted_routes: 61% said there is too much economic inequality.
The top response was 'too much' at 61%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 'Too much' slice/bar must be visibly labeled 61% and be the largest substantive response slice.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'most Americans said that there was too much economic inequality'
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state 61% for 'too much,' or is showing the largest slice without the number sufficient?

units.meaning: The 61% 'too much' share is a majority, i.e., more than half of respondents.

basis.note: 61% is above one-half; the majority threshold is implicit in the intent.

accepted_routes: A majority (61%) said there is too much economic inequality.
The majority response was 'too much' at 61%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must frame 'Too much' as the majority/more-than-half response, not merely as one slice among three.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'most Americans said that there was too much economic inequality'
units.reviewer_question: Must the animation explicitly frame 61% as a majority or more-than-half, separate from just being the largest slice?

units.meaning: About a quarter of respondents, 23%, said there is the right amount of economic inequality.
accepted_routes: 23% said the amount was about right.
About a quarter (23%) chose 'the right amount.'
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 'The right amount' slice must show 23% and be labeled as about a quarter if the narration references it.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'We also had about a quarter of Americans saying there was the right amount...'
units.reviewer_question: Must the video include the 'right amount' 23% category, or is it optional detail beyond the majority message?

units.meaning: The 'too little' response is 13%, which is lower than the 23% 'right amount' response; the gap is 10 percentage points.
accepted_routes: 13% said too little, compared with 23% who said the right amount.
Too little (13%) was less common than the right amount (23%).
The gap between 'right amount' and 'too little' is 10 percentage points.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the 'Too little' 13% slice and the 'The right amount' 23% slice must be visible if this comparison is made.
units.temporal_anchor: no narration clause; if shown, place after the right-amount clause as optional comparison.
units.reviewer_question: Should the 13% 'too little' category and its comparison with 23% be required, or is it optional context?

units.meaning: The 'too much' share, 61%, is larger than the combined shares of the other substantive response categories: 'right amount' (23%) plus 'too little' (13%) equals 36%, a difference of 25 percentage points.
accepted_routes: Too much (61%) exceeded the right amount plus too little combined (23% + 13% = 36%).
61% is larger than the other substantive response categories combined (36%).
The 'too much' share was 25 percentage points above the combined other response shares (61% - 36%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart or annotation must let viewers compare the 61% 'too much' slice against the combined 36% of the other substantive categories.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'most Americans said that there was too much economic inequality' as supporting comparison
units.reviewer_question: Must the video compare 'too much' against the combined other response categories, or is the majority framing alone sufficient?

optional_valid: Displaying the source annotation from the table: 'Survey of U.S. adults conducted Sept. 16-29, 2019.'
Showing the 'Too little' 13% slice as context even if the narration does not mention it.
Showing the 'The right amount' 23% slice as context for the 'about a quarter' narration clause.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not treat the 2.8% 'Source: Survey...' item as a substantive response category or as an 'other/don't know' response.
Do not claim the three printed response categories sum to 100% (61 + 23 + 13 = 97).
Do not explain causes of why people believe there is too much economic inequality.
Do not extrapolate beyond the survey source or claim all Americans without survey context.
notes: The core required message is that 61% chose 'too much' and that this is a majority. The right-amount, too-little, and combined-category comparisons are valid optional context; the 2.8% source item should not be treated as a response category.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
